item.title: Kazurabashi: The Iya Valley Vine Bridge — Guide
item.description: The Kazurabashi is one of the last surviving vine bridges in Japan, a remarkable suspension bridge in the Iya Valley woven entirely from the tough stems of mountain kiwi vines. Bridges like this once crossed the valley’s many gorges, built from natural materials that could be cut down quickly — legend says to foil pursuers in this refuge of defeated warriors. Around 45 metres long and swaying gently above the clear Iya River, the bridge is rebuilt every few years to keep it safe, but crossing it is still a genuine thrill: the vine ropes creak, the wooden slats are spaced with gaps you can see the water through, and the whole span moves as you go.
